title: How to Make Infused Olive Oil | The Bridge
description: The simplest infusion there is, with the shortest shelf life. A small adult batch of cannabis olive oil: keep it cold, label it, throw it out on day four.
lede: The simplest infusion there is, with the shortest shelf life. Make a small batch, keep it cold and throw it out on day four.
html:
Olive oil has a real pedigree here. Italian researchers studying pharmacist-prepared cannabis oil call it the first-choice concentrated preparation, and note that standard conditions for making it still aren't available. An Israeli storage study found olive oil the best of the vehicles it tested for preserving an extract's natural cannabinoids. If trained pharmacists are still working out the variables, expect your kitchen batch to vary too.

This one comes with a hard deadline. The CDC's botulism guidance says to refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs and throw them away after 4 days. Cannabis flower is an herb for this purpose, as far as we're concerned. That's why the batch is half the size you'd expect. For adults 21 and older, at home.

Ingredients

  • 1.75 grams cannabis flower (half an eighth)
  • 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil

You'll also need: a small baking dish, foil, an oven thermometer, an instant-read thermometer, a heatproof jar, a saucepan, a fine strainer or cheesecloth, a small bottle with a lid, a label and a lockbox.

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 240°F and confirm it with the oven thermometer.
  2. Break the flower up by hand into the baking dish, cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Here's why. Let it cool covered.
  3. Put the flower and oil in the heatproof jar. Stand the jar in a saucepan of water over low heat.
  4. Hold the oil between 160°F and 190°F for 90 minutes, stirring now and then. No bubbles, no smoke.
  5. Strain into the bottle and let it drip. Leave it to cool.
  6. Label it before it goes anywhere: CONTAINS THC, ADULTS ONLY, made on this date, throw out four days later.
  7. Refrigerate it in the lockbox. Olive oil can firm up in the cold, so let it soften and shake it well before each use, or the top and bottom may not match.

Using it

Finish with it. Don't fry with it. Lab work shows hotter and longer can start to lose THC, and there's no reason to risk that after the work you've put in. A few drops on your own plate is the idea, never the shared salad bowl. Nobody at your table should eat THC without knowing it.

The ceiling, and the first test

You can't measure this at home. All you can do is find the most it could hold: grams of flower, times 10, times the Total THC percent on the label. At 1.75 grams and 20%, that's 350 milligrams in the bottle. Half a cup is 24 teaspoons, so up to about 15 milligrams per teaspoon. New York limits a store-bought edible to 10 milligrams of THC per serving and says a new consumer may want to start at 2.5 to 5.

So start with a quarter teaspoon, under 4 milligrams even at that ceiling, on a day with nothing planned and nowhere to drive. Edibles may take up to two hours to feel and four or more hours to be fully felt. Fat can raise THC exposure as well: in one rat study, lipids increased it about 2.5 times. Have no more that day, and write down what happened.

Locked, and then gone

An unmarked bottle of olive oil is the most innocent thing in a kitchen, which is the problem. The Department of Health says infused products should never sit in a shared fridge or pantry near other food. Use the lockbox, keep it apart from the food, and if you can't guarantee that around kids, don't make this.

On day four it goes, however much is left. The state's disposal sheet says not to flush cannabis products down the sink or toilet. Mix the oil and the spent flower with coffee grounds or kitty litter, seal it in a container and put it in the regular trash. If anyone takes this by accident, call the Poison Center at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 in an emergency. For a pet, call your vet right away.
